matters.title: E. Resolution 2024-83 Approving the Engine Repairs for Fire Pumper
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jul 23, 2024 - July 23, 2024 Regular City Council Meeting 
 Category 
 6. New Business 
 Subject 
 E. Resolution 2024-83 Approving the Engine Repairs for Fire Pumper 
 Type 
 Action 

 Introduction: 
 One of the Hamtramck Fire Department's pumpers is in need of extensive repair to get it back into front-line service. 

 Overview: 
 The Hamtramck Fire Department had been having intermittent mechanical problems with one of its pumper trucks. The Fire Chief called our repair company, Apollo Fire Apparatus Sales and Service, which came out to diagnose the issue. They recommended that we take it to a Cummins dealer for a thorough diagnosis of the issue. Cummins had their certified technicians look at the pumper and diagnose the issue. They concluded that the issue was excessive blow-by and a plugged EGR system and it would need a new engine and EGR system. 

 The Chief subsequently contacted several other repair facilities and for various reasons, they are unable to perform the repairs. Wolverine Truck Group in Dearborn was then contacted, but they could not work on the truck based on the vehicle chassis. Tri-County Truck Repair was contacted, and the service manager stated they normally don’t handle this type of job referring us to Cummins. The Chief then spoke to Michigan Kenworth and they stated they are not able to do the repair. Apollo was again contacted for suggestions and their recommendation is to have Cummins do the repair based on them being the OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) their expertise, availability of parts, and repair warranty. 

 The repair is estimated to be $69,150.66 for parts and labor. It is estimated that the parts will take around 4 weeks to arrive and the repairs will start as soon as they arrive. This pumper is one of our two front-line pumpers and is critical for maintaining adequate fire protection for the City of Hamtramck. 

 Budget Impact: 
 The full cost of the repairs is $69,150.66 and is a general fund expense. 

 Recommendation: 
 To approve the engine and EGR repairs for the fire pumper at Cummins. 

 Prepared by: 
 Fire Chief, Matthew Wyszczelski 

 Reviewed by: 
 Max Garbarino, City Manager 

 Attachments: 
 Resolution 2024-83 Approving the Engine Repairs for Fire Pumper 
 Repair Estimate from Cummins of Dearborn 
 Letter from Apollo Fire Apparatus Sales and Service

matters.title: E. Resolution 2025-20 Approving the Purchase of New Dispatch Console for the Hamtramck Police Department
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Feb 25, 2025 - February 25, 2025 Regular City Council Meeting 
 Category 
 7. New Business 
 Subject 
 E. Resolution 2025-20 Approving the Purchase of New Dispatch Console for the Hamtramck Police Department 
 Type 

 Introduction: 
 This agenda item is a request for Council to approve the purchase of Motorola Solutions Avtec Scout Dispatch Console System for the Hamtramck Police Department. 

 Background: 
 The Hamtramck Police Department currently uses the Motorola MIP 5000 VOIP radio Console. The current dispatch console is having a lot of issues, and the system is no longer being supported. Parts are no longer available to make repairs if the system goes down. Motorola and Avtec end of release support was December of 2021. 

 This purchase of the Avtec Scout Dispatch Console is essential for the Police Departments operations. It will provide state-of-the-art equipment with a 10-year warranty for all the Dispatch consoles and equipment. It will also provide 2 computers that will always work and function if there are any issues that arise as a back-up to ensure there is no effect on the day-to-day operations of the dispatch system. 

 Budget Impact: 
 The cost of the purchase of the Motorola Solutions Avtec Scout Dispatch Console system is $345,613. Including in the cost is installation of all the new equipment, yearly maintenance on the radios and upgrades, removal of the existing console system, and a 10-year warranty all equipment including Hardware and any software. The Dispatch consoles will be purchased out of the Federal Narcotic fund. 

 Recommendation: 
 The City Manager and the Chief of Police recommend that the City Council approve the resolution for the purchase of Motorola Solutions Avtec Scout Dispatch Console System 

 Prepared by: 
 Andrew Mileski, Deputy Chief of Police 

 Reviewed by: 
 Maxwell Garbarino, City Manager 

 Attachments: 
 Service Quote for the New Radio Console and Warranty 
 Resolution 2025-20 Approving the Purchase of New Dispatch Console the Hamtramck Police Department

matters.title: B. Resolution 2026-151 Approving the Second Reading, Public Hearing, and Adoption of Proposed Ordinance Revision of Chapter 52 of the City of Hamtramck Code of Ordinances Regarding Fats, Oils, Grease, and Sediment Control
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Sep 22, 2026 - Regular City Council Meeting 
 Category 
 6. Public Hearing 
 Subject 
 B. Resolution 2026-151 Approving the Second Reading, Public Hearing, and Adoption of Proposed Ordinance Revision of Chapter 52 of the City of Hamtramck Code of Ordinances Regarding Fats, Oils, Grease, and Sediment Control 
 Type 
 Action 

 Introduction: 
 RES. 2026-151 APPROVING FIRST READING AND SETTING DATE FOR SECOND READING AND PUBLIC HEARING OF THE SECOND READING, PUBLIC HEARING, AND ADOPTION OF THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE TO AMEND CHAPTER 52, WASTEWATER, OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES OF THE CITY OF HAMTRAMCK BY ADDING A NEW SUBCHAPTER, FATS, OILS, GREASE, AND SEDIMENT CONTROL, §§ 52.100 THROUGH 52.116; TO REQUIRE THE INSTALLATION AND MAINTENANCE OF GREASE INTERCEPTORS AND OIL/WATER SEPARATORS; TO PROHIBIT CERTAIN DISCHARGES TO THE PUBLIC SEWER; TO PROVIDE FOR INSPECTION, MAINTENANCE, RECORDKEEPING, COST RECOVERY, AND ENFORCEMENT; AND TO PROVIDE FOR SEVERABILITY AND AN EFFECTIVE DATE. 
 Overview: 
 The City recognizes the importance of protecting the public sewer system from blockages, obstructions, and other conditions caused by the discharge or accumulation of fats, oils, grease, sand, grit, sediment, and similar substances. These materials can interfere with the operation of the City's sewer system, contribute to blockages and plugging of pipelines, interfere with pumps and controls, and contribute wastewater that may exceed the treatment capabilities of the wastewater treatment plant. 
 The proposed ordinance establishes a new Fats, Oils, Grease, and Sediment Control subchapter within Chapter 52, Wastewater. The requirements would apply primarily to food service establishments and automotive or industrial facilities, while also providing the City with authority to require appropriate control devices where other users discharge wastewater containing excessive grease, flammable wastes, sand, or other harmful ingredients. 
 Under the proposed ordinance, food service establishments would be required to install and maintain an approved grease interceptor or grease trap, while automotive and industrial facilities would be required to install and maintain an approved oil/water separator. The ordinance establishes standards for the design, sizing, installation, accessibility, and maintenance of these control devices. New control devices would require a permit through the City's Building Department and installation by an appropriately licensed contractor. 
 The ordinance also establishes prohibited discharge standards, including a limit of 100 mg/L for certain non-emulsified fats, wax, grease, starch, and oils, as well as a prohibition on the discharge of sand, rocks, grit, and other non-organic sediment or debris into the public sewer. It would also restrict the use of bacteria, enzymes, solvents, emulsifiers, and similar products in control devices without prior written approval from the Director. 
 Existing establishments that are lawfully operating without the required control devices would be provided a 12-month compliance period following the effective date of the ordinance to install required control devices and achieve compliance. Where an existing device is under-designed or substandard, the Director sets a compliance deadline of not more than six months. The ordinance also provides flexibility where installation of an outdoor interceptor is physically impossible or infeasible, allowing the Director to approve appropriate under-the-counter grease traps or other alternatives. Where an establishment's discharge has caused or contributed to a sewer blockage, obstruction, or interference, the Director may require an accelerated compliance schedule of not less than 30 days. 
 The proposed ordinance establishes ongoing maintenance and recordkeeping requirements. Grease interceptors and oil/water separators must be cleaned as necessary and at least once every three months unless otherwise approved by the Director, while under-the-counter grease traps must be cleaned weekly unless an alternative frequency is approved. Users would also be required to maintain maintenance schedules, cleaning and disposal records, manifests, and repair logs for at least three years. 
 The City would have authority to conduct inspections during normal business hours and to require corrective action where grease-handling facilities or practices are not adequately maintained. Following a written notice of violation, an establishment may also be required to must obtain independent testing and certification demonstrating that its control devices are functioning as intended every six months for two years, and the City may require more frequent testing after more than one notice of violation . 
 The ordinance further provides for cost recovery where a user's operations cause or contribute to excessive grease, sediment, or other obstructive material entering the public sewer, including costs associated with service calls, blockage removal, line cleaning, repairs, disposal, labor, materials, and equipment. Unpaid service-related charges may become a lien on the premises and may be certified for placement on the property tax roll in accordance with applicable law and the City Charter. 
 Following the first reading on September 8, 2026, the cost recovery section (§ 52.113) was revised to address Council's questions about new business owners and advance notice of charges. As revised, a new owner or operator is not liable for a condition that predates them. Where a blockage is attributable only in part to a business, the Department of Public Services must apportion the charges in writing and bill only that business's share. A property owner is liable, together with its tenant, for the share of a condition the tenant caused during the owner's period of ownership. Except in an emergency, the Department must inspect and record the condition on at least two separate dates and give at least 14 days' written notice, with an estimate of the charges, before performing billable work. After the work, the City issues an itemized invoice, which may be appealed in writing to the City Manager within 14 days after it is delivered or mailed. A timely appeal stays the payment deadline and any collection or enforcement action based on nonpayment of the disputed charges, including tax roll certification and discontinuance of service, until a decision is issued. It does not stay discontinuance for an independent continuing violation. The revision also clarifies that the 12-month compliance period runs from the effective date of the new subchapter, and that discontinued service will be restored once the violation is corrected and the person requesting restoration has paid the charges that person owes. The signature block now provides for the Mayor and City Clerk, consistent with Charter § 12-03. The revised text is attached in clean and redline form. 
 Violations would constitute municipal civil infractions subject to the City's established civil fine schedule or, where applicable, fines and costs provided by law. The ordinance also provides additional enforcement mechanisms, including injunctive relief, discontinuance of water and/or sewer service following continued or repeated violations or failure to pay service-related charges, and written notice and hearing procedures before service discontinuance. 
 Single-family and two-family residences would not be required to install grease interceptors, grease traps, or oil/water separators under the proposed ordinance. Residential users would, however, remain prohibited from discharging fats, oils, or grease to the public sewer and would be directed to collect cooking fats, oils, and grease for disposal with solid waste in accordance with the City's refuse collection requirements. 
 The ordinance also provides for limited variances and exemptions. The Director may approve alternatives to outdoor interceptors where installation is physically impossible or infeasible, and an establishment may qualify for an exemption from control-device requirements upon demonstrating that its discharge is below the applicable domestic background concentration. 
 Budget Impact: 
 The proposed ordinance is not expected to require a significant direct expenditure from the City. The primary costs associated with compliance—including the purchase, installation, cleaning, maintenance, testing, and repair of required grease interceptors, grease traps, and oil/water separators—would be the responsibility of the applicable property owner, leaseholder, or operator. 
 The ordinance does authorize the City to recover costs incurred when a user's discharge causes or contributes to a blockage or other condition requiring City response or corrective action. The City may also establish a periodic fee by resolution of City Council to cover costs associated with evaluation and review of required control devices. Administering the inspection, documentation, notice, billing, and appeal procedures in § 52.113 will require Department of Public Services and City Manager staff time, which has not been quantified. 
 Recommendation: 
 It is recommended that the City Council approve the first reading of the proposed ordinance and set the second reading and public hearing for September 22, 2026 hold the public hearing, approve the second reading, and adopt the proposed ordinance adding §§ 52.100 through 52.116 to Chapter 52, as revised after the first reading . 
 Prepared by: 
 Hamtramck DPS – Water & Sewer Division 
 Hamtramck Building Official, Bruce Eck 
 Hamtramck Building Department 
 Hamtramck CED
